title: Maryland's Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for U.S. Senate leadership post
summary: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate majority leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party…

image.caption: U.S. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he'll will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer. (Jose Luis Magana/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Updated

Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate majority leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections.
Van Hollen says Democrats 'need new leadership'
Van Hollen said in a statement that "the American people called for change" and that is why he is running.

"It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," Van Hollen said. "This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate Majority Leader."

Van Hollen's challenge comes after he said he was considering a bid and after Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December.
U.S. Sen. Chuck Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win. (Mariam Zuhaib/The Associated Press)
The race will be the first contested election for Democratic leader in decades.

The question of whether to re-elect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators will not say publicly how they will vote. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election, and Schumer recruited many of the party's winning candidates and raised money for them.
'I'm going to win it': Schumer
Schumer has been talking to Democratic senators since the election about forming an agenda for 2027.
"I'm going to win it," Schumer told The Associated Press in an interview last week.
In a statement after Van Hollen's announcement, Schumer said he welcomes any discussion about the future of the caucus.

"I'm proud of what we've accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader," Schumer said. "I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people."

While Schumer is the favourite to win, Van Hollen's run exposes a rift in the party that has put Schumer on the defensive since he sided with Republicans on a spending vote in March 2025. Even as he has redeemed himself within his caucus since then — leading them through a government shutdown last year and orchestrating huge wins in the election — many in the Democratic base are agitating for generational change.
Van Hollen, 67, is not that much younger than Schumer, 75. But he has positioned himself as a new face in the party. He has also said he is considering a run for president.
El-Sayed backs Van Hollen

While most Democratic senators have either said they are supporting Schumer or are undecided, Van Hollen has at least one backer in next year's caucus: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who won a competitive election in his state last week, posted on X Thursday night that their majority will need "bold leadership."
U.S. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is backing Van Hollen to be the Democrats' leader in the U.S. Senate. (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)

"I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience," El-Sayed wrote. "We need both right now. Which is why I'm proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority."
Several senators have said they are backing Schumer, including incoming Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown, who beat Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week.

Maine Sen. Angus King, an Independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the election, issued a statement after Van Hollen's announcement: "Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?
"Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible," King wrote.
